question: Establishment Democrat?
headline: Mixed
summary: House Democrats chose him as top Democrat on Oversight, 150–63, and he votes with most Democrats on nearly every roll call. But he is a Progressive Caucus member who took little money from party leaders' committees, none from Jeffries' or the DCCC, and broke with most Democrats on the January 2026 funding bills and a crypto-friendly IRS vote.
why: "Mixed" because the signs point both ways: party-line voting (rank 31 of 215 among House Democrats) and a leadership post voted by the caucus count as establishment; progressive-caucus membership, $4,000 from party leaders' committees in 2025–26 and breaks on funding bills count as independent.
tiles: From party leaders' committees in 2025–26, down from $15,000

e.text: Elected Democratic Caucus Leadership Representative (Nov 2024) and then Ranking Member of Oversight (Jun 2025), chosen by his colleagues 150-63.
Ranks 31 of 215 House Democrats for party-line voting on all roll calls.

i.text: Member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, and cosponsor of Medicare for All, the Raise the Wage Act and the Protecting the Right to Organize Act.

i.text: Party leaders' committees gave $15,000 in 2023–24 and $4,000 in 2025–26; Jeffries' committees and the DCCC gave nothing, per FEC records.
